title: The Moon and Her Mother
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: The Moon once begged her Mother to make her a gown. "How can I?" replied she; "there's no fitting your figure. At one time you're a New Moon, and at another you're a Full Moon; and between whiles you're neither one nor the other."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Moon beg her Mother to make?
According to the passage, what is the Mother's first reply to the request?
According to the passage, what does the Mother say there is no doing to the Moon's figure?
According to the passage, what is the Moon at one time?
According to the passage, what is the Moon at another time?
As the passage uses it, what does "fitting" mean in "there's no fitting your figure"?
options: Making clothes that match a shape

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Mother believe she cannot make the Moon a gown?
options: She does not know how to sew
The Moon's shape keeps changing, so no single gown could fit it
The Moon has refused every gown she has made before
She believes gowns are only for the Sun

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Mothers should always agree to their children's requests
The Moon is more beautiful than any gown could make her
Something whose shape is never fixed cannot be fitted with a single fixed garment
Gowns are unnecessary for anyone who lives in the sky

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who does the Moon beg to make her a gown?
According to the passage, what is the Moon between whiles, that is, between being new and being full?
options: Both a New Moon and a Full Moon at once

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what two phases does the Mother mention the Moon passes through?
options: A New Moon and a Full Moon
A Half Moon and a Crescent Moon
A Waxing Moon and a Waning Moon
A Blue Moon and a Harvest Moon

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "figure" mean in "there's no fitting your figure"?
options: The shape or outline of a body

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what can be inferred about the Moon's appearance over time?
options: It stays exactly the same every night
It constantly changes in size and shape
It only changes once a year
It disappears completely and never returns

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: The Moon's Mother happily agrees to sew her a gown at once
The Moon refuses a gown her Mother offers to make
The Moon asks for a gown, but her Mother explains her ever-changing shape makes it impossible to fit
The Moon and her Mother argue about which of them is more beautiful
